nodes.content: Develop long-tail image recognition that preserves rare-class accuracy when predictive background correlations reverse without target-domain labels.
requirements: Improve bottom-quintile class macro-accuracy by 5 percentage points over empirical risk minimization under background reversals.
Keep top-quintile class macro-accuracy within 1 percentage point of that baseline using identical training data.

nodes.content: Train a class-balanced tail adapter with self-supervised masks and within-training-set background swaps, distilling head logits from an ERM teacher.
Do self-supervised masks preserve rare-class object cues when swapping backgrounds, or do they erase features needed for recognition?
Masks retaining ≥90% foreground should enable swaps to lift tail macro-accuracy ≥5 points over ERM with ≤1-point head loss.
Audit mask retention against source-validation segmentation; compare filtered versus unfiltered swaps on LT-BackgroundFlip tail/head macro-accuracy without target labels.
Audit source-validation segmentation masks for ≥90% foreground retention; train filtered/unfiltered adapters and identical-data ERM, scoring LT-BackgroundFlip tail/head macro-accuracy.
With 92% foreground retention, LT-BackgroundFlip filtered swaps scored 35.1% tail macro-accuracy versus ERM's 32.0%; head fell 0.6 points.
Stratify filtered/unfiltered LT-BackgroundFlip errors by source-validation mask retention and discriminative-part occlusion; recompute tail/head macro-accuracy versus ERM.
With ≥97% foreground retention and intact diagnostic parts, tail macro-accuracy reached 38.2% versus ERM’s 32.0%; head dropped 0.7 points.
Does head-class logit distillation suppress tail gains from background swaps, despite protecting frequent-class accuracy?
Following the 92%-retention shortfall and ≥97%-retention success, sweep head-distillation weights {0,0.25,0.5,1}; compare tail/head macro-accuracy.
Retrain adapters on the 92%- and ≥97%-retention mask cohorts at head-distillation weights 0, 0.25, 0.5, and 1; measure tail/head macro-accuracy.
DistillationSweep-v1.csv lists eight adapter runs by mask-retention cohort and distillation weight, with LT-BackgroundFlip tail/head macro-accuracy and ERM deltas.
Train tail prototypes on source-only background-randomized crops; gate prototype corrections by calibrated tail probability, freezing ERM head logits.
Can source-calibrated tail gating prevent prototype corrections from misclassifying head-class images when backgrounds reverse?
A source-calibrated 0.8 tail-posterior gate will route fewer than 2% of LT-BackgroundFlip head images to tail prototypes.
Calibrate ERM tail posteriors on source validation; measure head-class prototype-routing rate at 0.8 on held-out LT-BackgroundFlip.
At the source-calibrated 0.8 gate, 1.4% of LT-BackgroundFlip head-class images routed to prototypes, below the hypothesized 2%.
Cluster source-only backgrounds; minimize tail worst-cluster loss while limiting head validation accuracy loss versus ERM to one point.
Cluster source backgrounds; compare worst-cluster tail models with and without head distillation under a one-point source-head accuracy constraint.

Use DistillationSweep-v1.csv to select distilled/undistilled settings; train worst-background-cluster adapters under one-point source-head constraint and measure LT-BackgroundFlip tail/head macro-accuracy.
WorstCluster-v1.csv records distilled and undistilled cluster-adapter settings, source-head constraint checks, and LT-BackgroundFlip tail/head macro-accuracy.
Audit WorstCluster-v1.csv; rerun compliant distilled/undistilled models across three seeds, testing ≥5-point tail gain and ≤1-point head loss versus ERM.
Across three seeds, source-head-compliant distilled worst-cluster models scored 38.0% LT-BackgroundFlip tail versus ERM's 32.0%; head fell 0.8 points.
Stress-test worst-cluster adapters on unseen backgrounds at 25%, 50%, and 100% reversal; compare tail/head macro-accuracy against identical-data ERM.
On held-out unseen-scene 100% reversals, worst-cluster tail macro-accuracy was 31.5% versus ERM's 29.4%; head fell 0.7 points.
Are source background clusters too coarse to cover unseen scenes, causing the 100%-reversal tail gain to shrink to 2.1 points?
Sweep source-background cluster counts {4,16,64}; compare unseen-scene embedding coverage and 100%-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy against ERM.
Against 38.0% LT-BackgroundFlip and 31.5% unseen-scene tail baselines, retrain 4/16/64-cluster adapters; measure centroid coverage and 100%-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy.
ClusterCoverage-v1.csv records 4/16/64-cluster unseen-scene embedding coverage and 100%-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy versus ERM.
Train source-only background-style diffusion to diversify tail prototypes beyond observed clusters, using calibrated tail gating to preserve ERM head predictions.
Compare source-only diffusion-diversified tail prototypes with 4/16/64-cluster adapters, measuring unseen-scene background coverage and 100%-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy.
Train source-only diffusion-diversified tail prototypes; benchmark 0.8-gated predictions against ClusterCoverage-v1.csv on unseen-scene coverage and 100%-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy.
Diffusion yielded 86% unseen-scene coverage versus clusters’ 68%; 100%-reversal tail macro-accuracy reached 35.1% versus ERM’s 29.4%, head −0.8 points.
Audit diffusion composites for altered diagnostic parts; rerun gated prototypes after rejecting damaged crops, comparing 100%-reversal tail/head macro-accuracy.
Rejecting 18% diagnostic-part-damaged diffusion crops reduced unseen-scene tail macro-accuracy to 33.7% versus ERM’s 29.4%; head fell 0.6 points.
Train source-only tail prototypes using ≥97%-retention crops and randomized background Fourier styles; source-calibrate correction gates, freezing ERM head logits.
Do Fourier background styles improve unseen-scene tail accuracy without the diagnostic-part damage observed in diffusion composites?
Fourier-styled, ≥97%-retention prototypes will achieve ≥34.4% unseen-scene tail macro-accuracy with ≤1% diagnostic-part damage and ≤1-point head loss.
Generate background-only Fourier styles on ≥97%-retention crops; audit diagnostic-part damage and benchmark 0.8-gated prototypes on unseen-scene tail/head macro-accuracy.
Train Fourier-styled tail prototypes from ≥97%-retention crops; audit diagnostic-part damage and score 0.8-gated unseen-scene tail/head macro-accuracy.
Fourier-styled prototypes achieved 34.8% unseen-scene tail macro-accuracy versus ERM’s 29.4%; diagnostic-part damage was 0.6%, head declined 0.7 points.
Freeze the validated Fourier settings and 0.8 gate; evaluate three-seed unseen-scene reversal intensities for tail/head macro-accuracy versus ERM.
Across three seeds, tail gains were 5.0/5.2/5.4 points at 25/50/100% unseen-scene reversals; head losses stayed ≤0.8 points.
Ablate Fourier styling and ≥97%-retention filtering using identical source images; compare unseen-scene tail/head macro-accuracy and diagnostic-part damage.
On held-out SceneShift-B 100% reversals, Fourier gained 3.8 tail macro-accuracy points versus ERM; no-Fourier gained 5.2, both head losses <1.
Does Fourier styling introduce source-specific frequency cues that explain its weaker tail accuracy on SceneShift-B?
Compare Fourier and no-Fourier prototype predictions across source-to-SceneShift-B frequency-distance bins, controlling object identity and mask retention.
Using three-seed Fourier results and SceneShift-B ablation predictions, match objects and ≥97%-retention masks; compare tail errors by source-frequency-distance quartile.
FrequencyAudit-v1.csv records matched-object SceneShift-B tail errors for Fourier/no-Fourier prototypes by source-frequency-distance quartile and mask retention.
Check FrequencyAudit-v1.csv matched-object completeness; estimate Fourier-minus-no-Fourier tail error gaps across frequency-distance quartiles with paired bootstrap intervals.
FrequencyAudit-v1: Fourier added 3.6 tail-error points in the highest frequency-distance quartile (95% CI 1.8–5.4), versus 0.1 in the lowest.
Drop Fourier styling despite reversal gains; retain ≥97%-retention prototypes and gating: SceneShift-B loses 1.4 tail points, high-frequency errors +3.6 points.
